goal: Make the head on the back view with the tail (third view) face away like the other back view, instead of turning to look over the shoulder, by adding turned-head negatives only.
why: Josh marked job 010 on-track and said: "On-track the third image should not have its head turned. Fix.it". The third view is the back view with the tail. In 010 seed 248 that head is turned in profile, with the muzzle, eye and mask showing over the shoulder; I misreported it as facing forward and it is turned. The same turn was in 009 seed 248, so it is not new. In 010's other three images the third-view head faces away (246 clean; 247 and 249 have only a goggle piece or strap on the back of the head). This is one change, negative only: '(looking back:1.3), looking over shoulder, (head turned:1.2)' is added at the end of 010's negative. These are the danbooru tags for the pose that gives a face on a back view, so telling the model to avoid them should leave the head as a back-of-head view. I chose the negative over strengthening the positive because the positive already says 'rear view, back view' and the parent's back views already face away; a negative leaves the positive identical to 010. I left out 'profile' and 'face visible from behind' because the side view is a real profile and the negative must not fight it. Risk: it might also change the side view or the front head tilt a little, and the head object faults in 247 and 249 are not addressed here. Everything else is exactly as in 010, so seed 248 compares with its twin: the locked less-human 246 parent, no charsheet LoRA, denoise 0.7, IP-Adapter ip-adapter-plus_sdxl_vit-h on the locked copy at 0.25 ending at 0.5, seeds 231506246-249 (4 images), Euler a, 30 steps, CFG 6, no hires, the same positive and the same other negatives. Check the third view's head in all four images, then the shading, eyes, symmetry and head ratio. No masks, guides or pixel edits.
